slides_filename: Ingest Pipeline Migration — Q3 Platform Review

contexts.general: Replaces the nightly batch load with a continuous stream. Unblocks three roadmap items that were gated on fresh data: live usage dashboards, alerting, and usage-based billing. Scope is ingest only — the warehouse schema is unchanged.
contexts.swe: Technical implementation: CDC over Kafka replaces batch ETL. Enables real-time data processing with sub-minute latency. Schema remains unchanged for backward compatibility.
contexts.marketing: Enables real-time features like live dashboards and usage-based billing. Improves customer experience by providing up-to-date data. Competitive advantage through faster insights.
contexts.executive: Reduces data staleness from 24 hours to under 90 seconds. Unblocks three strategic roadmap items. Approved budget for dual-write during cutover.
contexts.designer: User impact: Faster, more accurate data visualizations. Enables real-time dashboards that update as events occur rather than on a schedule.

components.text: Hover any highlighted text. The explanation rewrites itself for your discipline.

contexts.general: One artefact instead of three. The deck stops being a lowest-common-denominator document that under-serves every room it enters.
contexts.swe: Single source of truth for technical details. No more maintaining separate docs for different teams.
contexts.marketing: One deck serves all audiences. No need to create multiple versions for different stakeholders.
contexts.executive: Efficient knowledge sharing. One deck that adapts to different stakeholder needs saves preparation time.
contexts.designer: Consistent experience. Users see explanations tailored to their role without switching documents.

components.text: Replace nightly batch ETL with event-driven CDC over Kafka

contexts.general: Removes the up-to-24-hour staleness window that drives most 'why is my number wrong?' support tickets. Cost: an always-on streaming service to operate, versus a job that only ran at 2am.
contexts.swe: CDC over Kafka provides real-time data streaming. Reduces latency from hours to seconds. Requires always-on infrastructure.
contexts.marketing: Eliminates data staleness complaints from customers. Enables real-time product features that differentiate us from competitors.
contexts.executive: Reduces support ticket volume related to stale data. Infrastructure cost trade-off: always-on vs batch.
contexts.designer: User benefit: Near real-time data accuracy. Reduces confusion from outdated information.

components.text: Cut p99 ingest latency from 42 min to under 90 s

contexts.general: The 90-second target is what makes in-product alerting viable — below the threshold where a user would rather check the source system directly. We measured 42 min at p99 over the last quarter.
contexts.swe: p99 latency of 42 minutes is unacceptable for real-time systems. 90 second target achieved through optimized streaming architecture.
contexts.marketing: Sub-90-second latency enables real-time user notifications and alerts. Improves user engagement and satisfaction.
contexts.executive: 42 minute to 90 second improvement. Enables new product capabilities previously blocked by latency constraints.
contexts.designer: Performance improvement: Users experience near-instant updates. Reduces the need for manual refreshes.

components.text: Backfill via idempotent replay; dual-write during cutover

contexts.general: This is the de-risking step. Dual-write means we can abort the migration at any point and fall back to the old pipeline with no data loss — worth the extra two weeks of engineering time.
contexts.swe: Idempotent replay ensures data consistency during backfill. Dual-write provides rollback capability. Two-week engineering investment for risk mitigation.
contexts.marketing: Migration safety: Zero data loss guarantee. Allows confident communication of migration timeline to customers.
contexts.executive: Risk mitigation strategy: Dual-write enables safe rollback. Two weeks of engineering time is justified by the risk reduction.
contexts.designer: User protection: Data integrity maintained throughout migration. No disruption to end users.

components.text: Retire the nightly cron and deprecate the legacy Airflow DAGs

contexts.general: Removes roughly 9 engineer-hours a week of on-call toil. That capacity is already allocated to the Q4 alerting work, so the saving is real rather than notional.
contexts.swe: Eliminates legacy Airflow DAGs and cron jobs. Reduces operational complexity and maintenance burden by 9 engineer-hours weekly.
contexts.marketing: Engineering capacity freed up for feature development. 9 hours/week reallocated to Q4 roadmap items.
contexts.executive: Cost savings: 9 engineer-hours per week saved. Capacity reallocated to strategic Q4 initiatives.
contexts.designer: Operational improvement: More reliable systems with reduced maintenance overhead.

contexts.general: Measured at p99 against the June baseline. The 90 s figure is the target, not yet the observed value — current staging runs sit at 110 s and are still improving.
contexts.swe: p99 measurement: June baseline was 42 minutes. Target is 90 seconds. Current staging at 110s, optimization ongoing.
contexts.marketing: Performance improvement: From 42 minutes to 90 seconds. Enables near real-time user experiences.
contexts.executive: Key metric: p99 latency from 42 min to 90s. Target not yet met in staging (110s) but improving.
contexts.designer: User impact: Dramatic performance improvement. 42 minutes to 90 seconds is a 28x speedup.

contexts.general: Reclaimed on-call and manual-rerun toil, already committed to Q4 alerting. Worth stating as committed rather than available, or it will get spent twice.
contexts.swe: On-call reduction: 9 engineer-hours per week saved. Currently allocated to Q4 alerting development.
contexts.marketing: Resource allocation: 9 hours/week freed from operations. Already earmarked for Q4 roadmap.
contexts.executive: Efficiency gain: 9 engineer-hours/week saved. Committed to Q4 strategic initiatives.
contexts.designer: Capacity increase: More engineering time available for product improvements.

contexts.general: Live usage dashboards, in-product alerting, and usage-based billing. All three were gated on sub-minute data freshness; none can ship before this lands.
contexts.swe: Unblocked: Live usage dashboards, in-product alerting, usage-based billing. All required sub-minute data freshness.
contexts.marketing: Feature enablement: Three major features now possible with real-time data: live dashboards, alerting, usage-based billing.
contexts.executive: Strategic unlock: Three roadmap items dependent on this migration. Live dashboards, alerting, usage-based billing.
contexts.designer: Product expansion: Three new features enabled. Previously blocked by latency constraints.

components.text: Risk: dual-write doubles warehouse cost for the two-week cutover window. Finance has approved the overage.

contexts.general: The main open risk on the plan. Approved at ~£18k for the window. If cutover slips past two weeks the overage needs re-approval, which is the trigger to escalate.
contexts.swe: Cost risk: Dual-write doubles warehouse costs during cutover. £18k approved for 2-week window. Extension requires re-approval.
contexts.marketing: Budget consideration: Additional £18k approved for migration. Timeline risk if cutover extends beyond 2 weeks.
contexts.executive: Financial risk: £18k overage approved for 2-week window. Escalation trigger if timeline slips.
contexts.designer: Resource constraint: Temporary cost increase during migration. Managed within approved budget.
